auditor_value: sin 2θ = ½ gives θ = 15° or 75°; 15° is the listed option.

findings.quote: Mistaking ½ for the sine of 60° turns sin 2θ = ½ into 2θ = 120°, which gives θ = 60°.
findings.note: The stated cause does not produce the number named: a student who believes sin 60° = ½ would write 2θ = 60° and get θ = 30°, not 2θ = 120°. Reaching 120° needs a different confusion (with sin 150° = ½, or with sin 120°).
findings.fix: Writing 2θ = 120° instead of 30° or 150°, by confusing sin 120° (which is √3/2) with ½, gives θ = 60°.

findings.note: sin 2θ = ½ has a second solution in the launch range, 2θ = 150°, θ = 75°, which also gives half the maximum range; the line drops it without comment. Only 15° is among the options, so the answer stands, but the step should say so.
findings.fix: sin2θ = ½, so 2θ = 30° or 150°, θ = 15° or 75°; of these only 15° is among the options.

notes: R(15°) = R(75°) = R_max/2 checked. Option-2 mistake entry (forgetting to halve 2θ = 30°) is genuine.
